ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: this dispute cannot be settled on the evidence that exists, so it goes to a human reviewer, and the $6.00 fee stays on hold — neither collected nor refunded — while that review is pending.

What the record does establish. The trip record (EV-TRIP-00213) shows the driver marked arrival at the Jurong East bay at 17:47:05 and cancelled at 17:53:40 with reason RIDER_UNREACHABLE, that the trip was terminated by the driver with no boarding and no in-app calls, and that three chat messages existed. The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00213) shows the $6.00 fee is the greater of the TRANSPORT_HUB zone fee ($6.00) and the RYDE_X tier fee ($4.00), so it reconciles and POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged.

What is missing, and why it decides the case. The one instrument that decides a no-show charge — the driver's GPS trace (EV-GPS-00213) — is absent; the device never uploaded it (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT). The message export (EV-CHAT-00213) is also absent (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT), even though the trip record counts three messages, and the traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00213-01) is absent as well. POL-NS-01 requires all four conditions: the arrival event (a) is on the trip record, but limb (b) (the driver inside the 150 m TRANSPORT_HUB arrival radius at or before that event) and limb (c) (a continuous in-geofence dwell of at least 300 seconds, timed from the first qualifying fix and not from the arrival tap) can only be proved from the trace. With no trace, neither limb can be run: they are undecided, and an undecided limb supports neither the charge nor a refund. The driver is right that the trip record's own wait_time_min of 6.6 minutes is not the clause's dwell, because POL-NS-01(c) deliberately does not start the clock at the marker; the rider is right that limbs (b) and (c) are not made out, but that leaves them unproven, not disproved.

The rider's refund routes cannot run for the same reason. POL-NS-02 refunds only where the trace contains no qualifying in-radius fix — a trace that does not exist is not a trace containing no qualifying fix; it is impaired, not proof of absence. POL-NS-04(a) needs the content of the messages (and limb (c) would need a rider_track, which is absent and therefore undecidable and neutral, not adverse). POL-NS-05 needs a fix at the arrival timestamp. POL-NS-06 needs a measured dwell and, for limb (i), a present advisory. The rider's account of waiting from 5.45 and messaging three times, and the driver's account of waiting 5.47–5.53 and replying to every message, are uncorroborated by any instrument and neither is an admission against interest; the missing chat is neutral for both of you.

Confidence and escalation. Under POL-GEN-02(2) confidence is capped by the artifacts that carry the deciding facts — arrival, dwell and rider presence ride solely on the missing GPS and chat records at weight 0.0 — so the cap is 0.0, below the 0.70 floor. The case therefore escalates under POL-NS-09(a) (confidence below the floor), POL-NS-09(e) (the deciding fact rests solely on evidence impaired or missing) and POL-NS-09(c) (rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d each record 2 no-show disputes between this rider and this driver in the trailing 90 days, which the rider's own claim text confirms). Escalation is terminal: no refund and no driver payment issues, and the fee is held.

Not engaged. The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 3 (below the count limb of 4) and 3 of 107 completed trips is 2.8% (below the 8% rate limb), so compensation is not withheld on that ground, and lifetime counters such as prior_no_show_flags are context only and are not used. No referral is issued, because no clause on these facts produces one: POL-NS-05(ii) cannot run without a trace, and POL-NS-07's anti-farming branch does not fire.

Open questions for the reviewer: (1) whether the driver's device trace can be recovered, and if so whether it places him inside the arrival radius by 17:47:05 and holding for 300 seconds from the first qualifying fix; and (2) whether the three chat messages can be recovered, and if so whether they were locating messages from the rider and whether the driver replied within 120 seconds. Those answers settle the fee's chargeability and any driver compensation.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
